parameters.content:
## youtube-poster
Webhook-triggered posting workflow for YouTube. Unlike Graph API/Threads, YouTube Data API v3 can't just be handed a URL — it needs the actual video bytes uploaded via a **resumable upload session** (init call → PUT the bytes to the returned Location URL).

**OAuth is entirely the backend's job.** n8n only ever receives an already-valid `access_token` in the payload — refresh_token/client_id/secret never touch n8n, matching the per-call-token rule from websitePlan.md §5.

Because the video bytes (Download Video) and the upload session URL (Initiate Resumable Upload) come from two independent HTTP calls that don't depend on each other, they run in parallel and a **Merge** node combines them before the final binary PUT — an HTTP Request node's output replaces the item it received, so this is the standard n8n pattern for keeping binary data alive alongside a second API response.

**After importing:** activate the workflow, then:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:5678/webhook/youtube-poster \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "post_id": "pst_test004",
    "user_id": "usr_test",
    "platform": "youtube",
    "media_urls": ["https://.../video.mp4"],
    "youtube_metadata": {
      "title": "Test upload #smposting",
      "description": "Testing youtube-poster",
      "privacy": "private"
    },
    "token": { "access_token": "YOUR_VALID_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN" },
    "callback_url": "https://webhook.site/your-id"
  }'
```

`privacy` defaults to `private` if omitted — deliberately, so a test upload never accidentally goes public. For Shorts: same endpoint, just add `#Shorts` to the title/description and use a ≤60s 9:16 source video.

**Verify after import:** the 'Upload Video Binary' node's Body Content Type should be 'n8n Binary File' pointing at field `data` — double-check this specific dropdown, it's the one part of this workflow I couldn't test against a live n8n instance before handing it to you.
